skill.name: installing-skill-tracker
skill.description: Installs local Claude Code hooks that record skill usage events and prompt submissions, then provides verification and analysis scripts for project-level tracking.
skill.summary: Install local Claude Code hooks for skill usage tracking and verification.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: Most shell-command findings are false positives from Markdown fences or fixed jq/date parsing in generated hook scripts. The confirmed risk is that setup.py persistently changes .claude/settings.json to install Claude Code hooks. A semantic privacy risk remains because the installed prompt hook records full prompt text and session identifiers locally.

remediation.issue: Full prompt content is logged by the UserPromptSubmit hook.
remediation.suggestion: Log anonymized counts or skill names by default. Make full prompt logging opt-in and document retention clearly.
Show the planned hook changes before writing, back up existing settings, and provide an uninstall path.

remediation.issue: Local activity logs may be committed or shared by accident.
remediation.suggestion: Add .claude/activity-logs/ to ignore rules or warn users before creating logs.

remediation.issue: Generated shell hooks depend on jq and shell parsing.
remediation.suggestion: Validate jq before installation or replace shell parsing with Python scripts that use the json module.

semantic_findings.title: Full Prompt Content Logged Locally
semantic_findings.description: The UserPromptSubmit hook stores full prompt text with session identifiers in .claude/activity-logs/prompts.jsonl. Prompts may contain secrets or sensitive project information.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The generated hook explicitly extracts the prompt field and appends it to a local prompt log. This directly supports the privacy finding.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent Claude Code Hook Installation
semantic_findings.description: The setup script registers UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, and PostToolUse command hooks in .claude/settings.json. These hooks continue running during later Claude Code activity until removed.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file defines hook configuration and writes it into settings.json. That establishes persistent command execution for future Claude Code events.

content.value_statement: Teams cannot easily see which Claude Code skills are used or verified. This skill installs local hooks and reports project-level usage signals.
actual_capabilities: Registers UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, and PostToolUse hooks.
Logs prompt submissions and skill usage events to local JSONL files.
Verifies required directories, scripts, jq, and hook settings.
Generates a local usage analysis with invocation and failure counts.
limitations: Requires jq for the generated shell hooks.
Works only in projects that use Claude Code hook settings.
Stores prompt text locally unless the hook scripts are changed.
Does not provide remote dashboards, alerts, or synchronization.

use_cases.title: Measure Skill Adoption
use_cases.description: Track which local Claude Code skills are opened and used during project work.

use_cases.title: Verify Procedural Skills
use_cases.description: Record verification outcomes for skills that include setup and verify scripts.

use_cases.title: Find Unused Skills
use_cases.description: Compare installed skills with usage logs to identify skills that may need cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: Install Tracking Hooks
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup in a new project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up this skill tracker in my current project and run the verification checks.

prompt_templates.title: Check Existing Setup
prompt_templates.scenario: Confirm whether tracking is already installed.
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify whether the skill tracker hooks are installed and list any missing components.

prompt_templates.title: Review Usage Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the current skill usage logs and summarize invocations, failures, and unused skills.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Tracking Impact
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the installed hooks and explain what data they collect, where it is stored, and how to reduce sensitive logging.

output_examples.output: Directories and hook scripts are present. jq is available. The required Claude Code hook events are registered.

output_examples.input: Summarize skill usage for this project.
output_examples.output: The report lists total prompts, skill invocations, procedural skill results, unused skills, and high failure rates.

output_examples.input: Explain what data the hooks store.
output_examples.output: The hooks store prompt text, session identifiers, skill names, timestamps, and verification status in local activity logs.

best_practices: Run verification immediately after setup and after any settings change.
Review local activity logs before sharing or committing project files.
Tell project users that prompt text may be stored locally.
anti_patterns: Do not install it where prompt logging violates policy.
Do not commit .claude activity logs to source control.
Do not treat invocation counts as proof of successful skill outcomes.

faq.question: Does this skill send data to a remote service?
faq.answer: No evidence of network upload was found. The generated hooks write logs to local project files.

faq.question: What data is logged?
faq.answer: It can log prompt text, session identifiers, skill names, timestamps, and verification status.

faq.question: Can I use it without jq?
faq.answer: No. The generated shell hooks depend on jq to parse Claude Code hook input.

faq.question: Will it change my Claude Code settings?
faq.answer: Yes. The setup script updates .claude/settings.json to register hook commands.

faq.question: Is it useful for teams?
faq.answer: Yes, when teams need local skill usage signals and accept the prompt logging tradeoff.

faq.question: How should sensitive prompts be handled?
faq.answer: Disable prompt content logging or store only aggregated metadata when prompts may contain secrets.
